h1:
🍜 Michelin Bib Gourmand
Great Food, Gentle Prices
intro: Bib Gourmand is Michelin's badge for places that cook seriously good food without the fine-dining bill, and Thailand has 137 of them to work through. Start with Krua Apsorn's famously fat crab omelet packed with real crab for 120 baht, Khao Soi Mae Sai's rich spiced chicken khao soi at 55 baht a bowl, or the secret-marinade charcoal chicken at Kai Yang Saeng Thai in Nakhon Ratchasima. This is Michelin flavor you can walk in and order.
quickAnswerHtml: This guide gathers 137 Bib Gourmand restaurants across Thailand, led by Krua Apsorn and its legendary 120-baht crab omelet.

faq.q: Which Bib Gourmand should I try first?
faq.a: Krua Apsorn's Dusit branch is most people's first stop. Its thick, fluffy crab omelet is stuffed with real crab meat for 120 baht, made by a cook who has run the pan for over 25 years. Hard to beat for the money.
Khao Soi Mae Sai in Chiang Mai starts at 55 baht a bowl for chicken khao soi with a deep, spice-rich curry broth made from scratch. Little money, full flavor.

The crab omelet at Krua Apsorn, the loaded crispy-pork dry congee at Go Benz in Phuket, and the charcoal-grilled chicken at Kai Yang Saeng Thai in Nakhon Ratchasima capture what Bib Gourmand Thailand is all about.

faq.q: Which provinces have the most Bib Gourmand spots?
faq.a: Bangkok leads with around 32, followed by Phuket with 19 and Chiang Mai with 18. The rest spread across Khon Kaen, Surat Thani, Ayutthaya, Nakhon Ratchasima and more.

faq.q: Which places should I book ahead?
faq.a: Most are walk-in spots, but favorites like Krua Apsorn and Kai Yang Saeng Thai pack out at lunch and on weekends, so arrive early or call ahead to check the wait.
